ra: Ignatius of Loyola founded and led the Society of Jesus (1540).
Francis Xavier was a founding companion of the Society of Jesus.
Peter Faber was a founding companion of the Society of Jesus.
Francis Borgia was the third Superior General of the Society of Jesus.
Peter Canisius was a leading early Jesuit.
Robert Bellarmine was a Jesuit cardinal and theologian.
Aloysius Gonzaga was a Jesuit novice.
Stanislaus Kostka was a Jesuit novice.
Peter Claver was a Jesuit missionary at Cartagena.
Isaac Jogues was a Jesuit missionary in New France.
Jean de Brébeuf was a Jesuit missionary to the Huron.
Isaac Jogues is one of the eight North American Martyrs.
Jean de Brébeuf is one of the eight North American Martyrs.
Teresa of Ávila founded the Discalced Carmelite reform.
John of the Cross co-founded the Discalced Carmelite reform.
Teresa of Ávila and John of the Cross were co-reformers of the Carmelite order and spiritual collaborators.
Vincent de Paul and Louise de Marillac jointly founded the Daughters of Charity.
Francis de Sales and Jane Frances de Chantal jointly founded the Order of the Visitation.
Jane Frances de Chantal was the spiritual disciple of Francis de Sales, her director.
Francis Xavier was formed by Ignatius of Loyola and made the Spiritual Exercises under him.
Peter Faber was a first companion formed by Ignatius of Loyola.
Martín de Porres and Rose of Lima were contemporary Dominican holy figures of colonial Lima.
Ignatius of Loyola and his order embody the Counter-Reformation missionary impulse.
Francis Xavier is the patron saint of the missions.
Peter Claver is patron of missionary work, especially African missions.
Turibius of Mogrovejo led the evangelizing reform of colonial Peru.
Teresa of Ávila is a Doctor of the Church on contemplative prayer.
John of the Cross is a Doctor of the Church on contemplative prayer and mysticism.
Francis de Sales taught lay devotional prayer in the Introduction to the Devout Life.
Camillus de Lellis is patron of the sick, hospitals and nurses.
John of God is patron of hospitals and the sick.
Martín de Porres is venerated as a healer and patron of the infirm.
Vincent de Paul is patron of charitable works for the poor.
Louise de Marillac is patroness of social workers and service to the poor.
Benedict Joseph Labre is patron of the homeless and the destitute.
Peter Canisius, Doctor of the Church, is patron of catechists and Catholic education.
Robert Bellarmine, Doctor of the Church, is patron of catechists and canonists.
Alphonsus Liguori, Doctor of the Church, is patron of confessors and moral theologians.
Isaac Jogues is venerated as a martyr of the North American missions.
Jean de Brébeuf is venerated as a martyr of the North American missions.
Josaphat Kuntsevych is venerated as a martyr for church unity.
The North American Martyrs are a devotional collective venerated for martyrdom.
Our Lady of Guadalupe is a Marian apparition and title of Mary Theotokos venerated in the Americas.
Rose of Lima, Dominican mystic, is venerated as a model of penitential contemplative prayer.
Catherine dei Ricci was a Dominican mystic loosely associated with Counter-Reformation Carmelite spirituality; weak link pending a Dominican hub.
Mary Magdalene de' Pazzi was a Carmelite nun of the Counter-Reformation era.
Philip Neri, founder of the Oratory, is a patron of joyful Catholic devotion and prayer.
Charles Borromeo led the pastoral implementation of Tridentine reform.
Aloysius Gonzaga, who died nursing plague victims, is patron of the sick in epidemics.
Paul of the Cross founded the Passionists devoted to meditation on the Passion.
Joseph of Cupertino was a Franciscan mystic noted for ecstatic prayer.
Jane Frances de Chantal co-founded the contemplative Visitation order.
Alphonsus Liguori and Paul of the Cross were contemporary 18th-century Italian founders of Passion-centered congregations.
Francis Borgia was drawn into the Jesuits after making the Spiritual Exercises under Peter Faber.
Stanislaus Kostka is patron of novices and Catholic youth, models of devotion.
